scope: Native iPhone Simulator Month date selection, Today return, collapsed day navigation and exact-task route; largest-text Year regression.
productChanges: Accessibility Month view uses full-width wrapping weekday/date rows and task counts instead of clipping a seven-column grid. Vertical row scrolling keeps Month expanded.
Month opens at the selected date. Today reveals its date even when already selected; a stable toolbar identifier supports the native check.
Normal Month cells have a 48-point minimum height, with the pager and scaled weekday header sized to fit all six weeks.
Accessibility period title wraps above period navigation. The collapsed calendar shows a measured full date plus Previous day/Next day controls instead of seven clipped dates.
Selected-day summaries wrap, use a shorter date and scaled caption at accessibility sizes; the empty summary says No tasks so the floating add button does not obscure Nothing planned.
build: Build-for-testing v7 succeeded. Genuine Apple Development signing receipt ios-month-route-signing-v4.json; signing checks enabled.
accepted: v3 normal/light Month: first and last date targets >=44x44, selected traits, Today return, exact task title, Cancel and normal relaunch retaining both open Today tasks.

v4 accessibility XXXL/dark Month: first and last full rows reachable, selected, >=44x44 and fully inside the viewport; empty summary No tasks; Today returns the entire row without extra scrolling after scrolling away while today remains selected; exact count 2 tasks.
v4 collapsed largest: full selected-date accessibility label, actual Previous day then Next day, original date return, exact original task title, Cancel/relaunch and retained open tasks.

v3 accessibility XXXL/dark Year: all twelve full month rows reachable inside the scroll viewport, selected current month opens Month, today selected, exact task route and retained open tasks after relaunch.
acceptanceBuildLimits: v3 normal Month and Year ran on build v6. Final build v7 changes only the zero-task accessibility summary wording and adds its assertion; v4 re-executes the affected largest Month case. Normal summary text and Year tested two-task summary are unchanged.
intermediateResults: v1 largest baseline fails its first target-height assertion: an empty date is 38 points high. Its inspected capture shows severely clipped two-digit dates, weekday labels and month/year title.
v2: normal Month passes, largest Month return-to-today and Year March containment fail. These remain failed evidence; captures alone do not override failed hit/viewport checks.

v3: all three pass after selected-date/Today restoration, shorter summary, and slow centered drags replacing edge gestures. The selected empty-day capture still shows Nothing planned partly obscured by the floating add button.
v4: the affected largest Month case passes after No tasks wording and a new native summary assertion.
limits: iPhone Simulator only; no new iPad, physical device, Mac runtime or spoken VoiceOver acceptance.
The Month walk selects first, last and today; it does not individually render/audit every date or every locale.
Some immediately-after-selection captures include in-progress text transitions. The stable v3 collapsed-date capture is also retained; its layout is unchanged by the final zero-task caption edit.
Current normal Month and largest selected-date/Today/collapsed captures are visually inspected. Current Year October is visually inspected; all twelve Year rows have native hit/viewport checks.
Full Day/3 days/5 days/Week large-text layouts and broader task-list usability remain open.
The prior unfiltered capture/editor accessibility audit remains failing with two normal and two largest clipping findings; it was not rerun unchanged.
Console Apple WebKit/WebCore duplicate-class and debugger-version warnings remain; structured runtimeWarnings are retained below.
No persistence, sync, widget or release contract changed. Mac receives evidence/docs only; its independent desktop calendar implementation is unchanged.

storage.retained: Original xcresults, logs, summaries, signing receipts, manifests, scoped captures and the two in-flight v2 diagnostic screenshots
